phases.name: Attendance, leave, and deductions

phases.name: Payroll engine

phases.name: Payroll operations

phases.name: Payslips, reports, and dashboard

phases.name: Data exchange

phases.name: Hardening
phases.objective: Verify tenant isolation, sensitive-data handling, accessibility, responsive behavior, and query shape on the built flows.

phases.name: Release readiness

tasks.title: Replace the single environment login with stored users
tasks.description: Sign-in compares one username and password from environment variables, then writes a session with company c1 and role owner for every login.
tasks.output: DEC-018 stores users with scrypt hashes, memberships, and a session version. The cookie holds user id, company id, and version; each request resolves the role from the membership. The first successful environment sign-in creates the account owner when the store has no users, and later environment password changes do not replace the hash. Failures are rows in the store. A password change increments the version, and replacePassword clears the cookie. The password form is S-041. Creating a company adds the account owner as Owner (S-005). The header switch accepts only a membership company. Review: no statutory formula, hashes and audit omit the password, and a viewer can sign in only for their companies.

tests.result: 5 passed in users tests: the first environment sign-in creates an owner of every company and a later environment password does not replace the hash, a viewer signs in as a viewer and only sees their companies, eight failures lock the username until the window passes including after a JSON round trip, a password change ends the previous session and the audit omits the password, and sign-in is unconfigured when the store has no user and no environment login.

done: The session is an HMAC-signed, httpOnly cookie, secure in production, with constant-time comparison.
Store users with a scrypt password hash and a list of company memberships.
The session carries the user id and version, and each request resolves the role from the membership. A viewer can sign in.
Failed sign-ins are stored, so a restart does not clear the lockout.
Sign-out deletes the cookie. A password change increments the session version, and replacePassword also deletes the cookie.
